cards.front: force
cards.back: A push or a pull.
cards.say: force. A push or a pull.

cards.front: What are the two main kinds of force?
cards.back: Pushes and pulls.
cards.say: What are the two main kinds of force? Pushes and pulls.

cards.front: What do we measure force in?
cards.back: Newtons (N).
cards.say: What do we measure force in? Newtons.

cards.front: What tool measures force?
cards.back: A newton meter, also called a force meter or spring balance.
cards.say: What tool measures force? A newton meter, also called a force meter or spring balance.

cards.front: What can a force do to an object?
cards.back: Start it moving, stop it, change its speed or direction, or change its shape.
cards.say: What can a force do to an object? Start it moving, stop it, change its speed or direction, or change its shape.

cards.front: Opening a door by pulling the handle uses what?
cards.back: A pull.
cards.say: Opening a door by pulling the handle uses what? A pull.

cards.front: Kicking a football uses what?
cards.back: A push.
cards.say: Kicking a football uses what? A push.

cards.front: friction
cards.back: A force that happens when two surfaces rub together. It slows things down.
cards.say: friction. A force that happens when two surfaces rub together. It slows things down.

cards.front: Which surface gives more friction, carpet or ice?
cards.back: Carpet. Ice is very slippery.
cards.say: Which surface gives more friction, carpet or ice? Carpet. Ice is very slippery.

cards.front: Which surface gives less friction, polished floor or rough road?
cards.back: Polished floor.
cards.say: Which surface gives less friction, polished floor or rough road? Polished floor.

cards.front: Why do shoes have grooves on the bottom?
cards.back: Grooves give more friction so we do not slip.
cards.say: Why do shoes have grooves on the bottom? Grooves give more friction so we do not slip.

cards.front: Why do we put oil on bike chains?
cards.back: Oil reduces friction so the parts move easily.
cards.say: Why do we put oil on bike chains? Oil reduces friction so the parts move easily.

cards.front: What does friction do to a moving toy car?
cards.back: It slows the car down until it stops.
cards.say: What does friction do to a moving toy car? It slows the car down until it stops.

cards.front: Why does rubbing your hands together make them warm?
cards.back: Friction makes heat.
cards.say: Why does rubbing your hands together make them warm? Friction makes heat.

cards.front: Why do car tyres have patterns?
cards.back: The pattern grips the road, giving more friction.
cards.say: Why do car tyres have patterns? The pattern grips the road, giving more friction.

cards.front: Which makes a toy car go further, a smooth floor or a rough floor?
cards.back: A smooth floor, because there is less friction.
cards.say: Which makes a toy car go further, a smooth floor or a rough floor? A smooth floor, because there is less friction.

cards.front: Name a force that pulls everything down.
cards.back: Gravity.
cards.say: Name a force that pulls everything down. Gravity.

cards.front: gravity
cards.back: A force that pulls objects towards the ground.
cards.say: gravity. A force that pulls objects towards the ground.

cards.front: True or false: There is friction between your shoes and the floor when you walk.
cards.back: True. Friction helps your shoes grip the floor so you do not slip.
cards.say: True or false: There is friction between your shoes and the floor when you walk.. True. Friction helps your shoes grip the floor so you do not slip.

cards.front: Is friction useful?
cards.back: Yes. It helps us walk, grip and stop, but it can also wear things out.
cards.say: Is friction useful? Yes. It helps us walk, grip and stop, but it can also wear things out.

cards.front: Which needs a bigger force, moving a bus or moving a toy?
cards.back: Moving the bus. Heavier objects need bigger forces.
cards.say: Which needs a bigger force, moving a bus or moving a toy? Moving the bus. Heavier objects need bigger forces.

cards.front: Which direction does friction push?
cards.back: Against the way an object is moving.
cards.say: Which direction does friction push? Against the way an object is moving.

cards.front: A heavy box is hard to push over a floor. What force is acting against you?
cards.back: Friction between the box and the floor.
cards.say: A heavy box is hard to push over a floor. What force is acting against you? Friction between the box and the floor.
